narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you received other job offers while working here, and how long you have been with this current organization. These stood out as the strongest drivers compared to everything else in your profile.

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years pushed the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, half had only 1-5 years of experience, so your longer background made you appear more mobile and likely to explore new opportunities. Similarly, having received other job offers during your time here strongly increased the chance of leaving, as this is relatively uncommon among those predicted to stay. Finally, your 1-5 years in this specific role also contributed to the prediction of departure. Most employees the model thought would remain had similar short-to-medium tenure here, suggesting this period often coincides with people reassessing their future.

The organization should review how it retains experienced staff who are receiving external offers. You may want to reflect on whether your current path still aligns with your goals or if exploring those other opportunities would be better. Addressing these mobility signals early could help retain talent like you. (248 words)
